index.faq.a1: No. UCPlan is an independent project. It is not affiliated with the University of California or with ASSIST. Transfer data comes from public ASSIST reports.
index.faq.a2: No. UCPlan is a planning aid. Admission decisions belong to the UC campuses. Nothing here promises or predicts an admission outcome.
index.faq.a3: Six campuses participate in the Transfer Admission Guarantee (TAG): UC Davis, UC Irvine, UC Merced, UC Riverside, UC Santa Barbara, and UC Santa Cruz. UCLA, UC Berkeley, and UC San Diego do not offer TAG.
index.faq.a4: Nothing right now. The free tools stay free. A Pro plan later will add new features only; current features will not be taken away.
index.faq.a5: No. The free tools work without signing up. An account system will arrive with Pro. Until then, a plan made in UC Course Planner is saved only in this browser — switching devices or clearing browser data will lose it.
index.faq.a6: Transfer-OS covers 50 California community colleges × 6 UC campuses. UC Course Planner covers programs at UC Irvine, UC San Diego, and UC Santa Barbara, and coverage keeps growing.

index.meta.desc: UCPlan offers two free tools that help California community college students plan their transfer to UC: Transfer-OS for the whole path, and UC Course Planner for semester-by-semester courses.

index.pro.p1: The tools you see today stay free. A Pro plan later will add only new features: TAG tracking, deadline reminders, comparing multiple plans, application-season checklists, and progress export. One account and one payment will unlock Pro in both tools. No prices yet — Pro will be announced when it is ready.
index.pro.p2: Public ASSIST data itself is never charged for.
